open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence identity across backup restoration
open_points.text: “one more than the last its store ever wrote; never reused in that store” contradicts “A store the owner restores from a backup continues from the backup's last number; the entries written after the backup are lost with it and exist nowhere.”
open_points.question: After restoring a backup whose last sequence is N, when the same store had previously written later entries, does the next entry reuse N+1, preserve the pre-restore high-water mark, or belong to a new store identity against which sequence numbers are scoped?
options: Reuse numbers from the discarded post-backup branch and define “ever wrote” only over the restored surviving history
Preserve a high-water mark outside the backup so no number the store previously issued is reused
Treat the restored store as a new identity or lineage, allowing the same sequence numbers only across distinct stores
open_points.default_guess: The restored history replaces the lost branch, so the next entry is the backup's last number plus one and may reuse a number issued only in the discarded branch.
